status: Both complete first-seed1ns panels and primary, full-path, temporal-order, amplitude-bin and bond-horizon diagnostics completed
paired_arrays: Mean candidate-minus-reference,95percent system-bootstrap lower,upper; exploratory marginal intervals

A_query_horizon.interpretation: Nonmonotonic early queries, with pronounced last-query degradation. Much less severe than B, but neither recipe preserves geometry at distant queries. Joint-window generation, not autoregressive rollout accumulation. No proven time-embedding root cause.

temporal_order.interpretation: Chronological-versus-exact-permutation variogram ratios are not universally higher-is-better. B overstates average lag1/lag4 order relative to MD while geometry fails; horizon-dependent drift or variance can also generate an order signal. Native BioKinema's much smaller lag1 signal is retained as contrary evidence to a blanket external-model superiority claim. No dynamics or kinetics equivalence established.

motion_bins.interpretation: B has worse bond and RMSF errors in all bins and excess fluctuation in low/medium-motion conditions. Its high-motion MSD difference from A is unresolved, not evidence B wins large-motion tasks. A still underfluctuates in the high bin. Systems may occur in multiple bins through different anchors.

full_path_analysis.status: completed, all96 conditions/192 forecasts per model, zero extra neural calls; original serial analysis retains its separate output
full_path_analysis.metric: Fair finite-ensemble energy scores of full12-frame CA paths; lower-is-better; two draws per condition, not equilibrium or force-field energies
full_path_analysis.interpretation: A improves all four full-path scores versus h/v, reinforcing rather than erasing its RMSF/MSD benefits despite worse all-atom geometry. Versus BioKinema, A improves distance-increment paths but worsens position paths; other two differences are unresolved. B improves position/distance paths versus h/v but worsens distance-increment paths. Only the distance-increment score clearly favors A over B among these four A/B scores. CA distribution scores do not certify all-atom geometry, thermodynamics or kinetics.

decision: Retain both unchanged second seeds and matched static-to-MD stages. A performs better than B on listed1ns errors but is not a joint geometry/motion improvement over h/v, and neither is geometrically competitive with native BioKinema. No promotion or inference-time clipping. Future interventions must distinguish temporal-conditioning extrapolation from denoising/geometry capacity rather than attribute the failure by model name.
